title: Soil Types in East Africa — Characteristics and Management
content:
## Common Soil Types in East Africa

### 1. Red Volcanic Soils (Nitisols/Ferralsols)

**Location:** Kenya highlands (Central, Rift Valley), Kilimanjaro region (Tanzania), Rwanda, Burundi

**Characteristics:**
- Deep, well-drained, red to dark red color
- Good structure — does not crack or become waterlogged
- Moderate to high natural fertility
- pH typically 5.0–6.5 (slightly acidic to neutral)
- Excellent for tea, coffee, maize, beans, vegetables

**Management:**
- Lime if pH <5.5: apply 1–2 t/ha agricultural lime
- Respond well to phosphorus additions (P tends to be fixed in acidic conditions)
- Mulching retains moisture and prevents erosion

### 2. Black Cotton Soils (Vertisols)

**Location:** Rift Valley floor (Lake Naivasha area), northern Tanzania plains, parts of Uganda

**Characteristics:**
- Black to dark grey; very high clay content (>40%)
- Cracks deeply in dry season; very sticky when wet
- High water-holding capacity but poor drainage
- High natural fertility (calcium, magnesium) but poor structure
- Difficult to work with machinery or hand tools in wet conditions

**Best crops:** Cotton, sorghum, sunflower, maize (if drainage managed)

**Management:**
- Raised bed planting to improve drainage
- Work soil when slightly moist — not too wet or too dry
- Avoid heavy machinery when wet (compaction risk)
- Gypsum application (1–2 t/ha) improves structure

### 3. Sandy Loam Soils (Coast/Lowland)

**Location:** Kenya/Tanzania Coast, Lake Victoria basin lowlands

**Characteristics:**
- Light texture; drains quickly
- Low water retention — drought stress risk
- Often low fertility; nutrients leach easily
- pH typically 5.5–7.0

**Management:**
- Frequent small applications of fertilizer (rather than one large dose)
- Heavy organic matter addition (compost, manure) to improve water retention
- Drought-tolerant varieties essential
- Micro-irrigation (drip) is most water-efficient

### 4. pH Management

**Target pH for most crops: 6.0–6.5**

| pH range | Status | Action |
|----------|--------|--------|
| <5.0 | Very acidic | Apply 3–4 t/ha agricultural lime |
| 5.0–5.5 | Acidic | Apply 1–2 t/ha agricultural lime |
| 5.5–6.5 | Good | Maintain with organic matter |
| >7.5 | Alkaline | Add sulfur or acidifying fertilizer |

**How to lime:** Apply well before planting (3–4 months if possible); incorporate into top 15cm; do not mix lime directly with DAP/CAN (chemical reaction). Cost: ~USD 80–120/t delivered in East Africa.
content_sw:
## Aina za Udongo Afrika Mashariki

### Udongo Mwekundu (Volcanic)

Unapatikana: milima ya Kenya (Kati, Bonde la Ufa), Kilimanjaro. Una kina, unadrainish vizuri, rutuba nzuri. pH 5.0–6.5.

### Udongo Mweusi (Black Cotton)

Unapatikana: sakafu ya Bonde la Ufa, kaskazini Tanzania. Una udongo mwingi, hufuatika wakati wa kiangazi, na kuwa tope wakati wa mvua.

### Usimamizi wa pH

PH bora: 6.0–6.5. Kama pH <5.5: weka chokaa (tani 1–2/hekta).

title: Arusha Red Volcanic Soil — Preparing for Commercial Tomato
content:
## Arusha / Northern Tanzania — Red Volcanic Soil for Tomatoes

Arusha, Meru, and Moshi sit on young volcanic parent material. Soils are typically deep red or dark reddish-brown nitisols — excellent for horticulture when managed correctly.

### Typical properties near Arusha

- **Texture:** Clay-loam to clay; good structure when organic matter is maintained
- **Drainage:** Naturally good on slopes; flat plots may need raised beds
- **pH:** Often 5.2–6.2 (slightly acidic). Target 6.0–6.5 for tomato
- **Nutrients:** Moderate N; phosphorus often limited (fixed in acid soils); potassium variable
- **Water:** Borehole irrigation is common — drip systems cut disease pressure vs overhead sprinklers

### Field preparation for first-season commercial tomato (2 acres ≈ 0.8 ha)

1. **Soil test** (county/extension lab if available): pH, N, P, K, organic carbon
2. **Clear and plough** 20–30 cm deep; remove previous crop residues that hosted bacterial wilt
3. **Lime** if pH <5.5: 1–2 t/ha agricultural lime, incorporate 3–4 weeks before transplanting
4. **Organic matter:** 10–20 t/ha well-rotted manure or compost — critical on volcanic soils that lose structure under continuous tillage
5. **Basal fertilizer at transplant:** DAP 100–150 kg/ha (or 5–10 g DAP per planting hole)
6. **Beds:** Raised beds 15–20 cm high, 1 m wide beds with 40–50 cm paths — improves drainage in heavy rain and keeps roots warmer

### Irrigation on borehole water

- Prefer **drip** (1–2 L/hour emitters, 1–2 lines per bed)
- Avoid waterlogging — volcanic clay holds water; over-irrigation causes root rot and bacterial wilt spread
- Mulch with dry grass or black plastic to reduce evaporation and soil splash (late blight spores)

### Rotation warning

Do not plant tomato after potato, eggplant, pepper, or previous tomato on the same plot without a 2–3 year break if bacterial wilt is present in the area.
content_sw:
## Udongo Mwekundu wa Arusha — Maandalizi ya Nyanya za Biashara

Arusha, Meru, na Moshi zina udongo wa volkano — nyekundu, wenye kina, mzuri kwa mboga kama unasimamiwa vizuri.

### Sifa

- pH mara nyingi 5.2–6.2 — lengo 6.0–6.5 kwa nyanya
- Fosforasi mara nyingi ni shida (imefungwa katika udongo asidi)
- Maji ya kisima yanafaa; tumia **drip** ili kupunguza magonjwa

### Maandalizi (ekari 2 ≈ hekta 0.8)

1. Pima udongo (pH, N, P, K)
2. Lima sentimita 20–30; ondoa mabaki ya mazao ya familia ya nyanya
3. Chokaa tani 1–2/hekta kama pH <5.5
4. Samadi/compost tani 10–20/hekta
5. DAP kilo 100–150/hekta wakati wa kupandikiza
6. Vitanda vilivyoinuliwa sentimita 15–20

### Tahadhari

Usipande nyanya baada ya viazi, biringanya, au pilipili kwenye shamba moja bila kupumzisha miaka 2–3 ikiwa kuna bacterial wilt.

title: Organic Matter, Erosion Control, and Lime for Smallholders
content:
## Building Soil Health on Smallholder Farms

### Organic matter targets

- Aim for ≥2% organic carbon in topsoil for vegetable and maize systems
- Apply 5–10 t/ha compost or well-rotted cattle/goat manure each season if available
- Never apply raw manure directly under tomato seedlings — burns roots and spreads pathogens; compost 6–8 weeks first

### Simple compost recipe (farm-scale)

- Mix 3 parts dry crop residue : 1 part fresh manure : water to damp sponge feel
- Turn every 2 weeks; ready in 6–10 weeks in warm East African climates

### Erosion control (highlands and volcanic slopes)

- Contour ploughing and trash lines (crop residue on contour)
- Napier or vetiver grass strips every 10–20 m on slopes >5%
- Mulch bare soil after harvest — red volcanic soils lose topsoil fast in March–May rains

### Lime timing

- Apply lime in the dry season before long rains; incorporate into top 15 cm
- Do not mix lime in the same hole with DAP or CAN on transplant day
content_sw:
## Rutuba ya Udongo, Mmomoa, na Chokaa

### Lengo

- Ongeza samadi/compost tani 5–10/hekta kila msimu
- Usitumie samadi mbichi chini ya miche ya nyanya — choma mizizi na kusambaza magonjwa

### Kudhibiti mmomoa

- Lima kulingana na kontua
- Panda nyasi za Napier/vetiver kwenye miteremko
- Funika udongo baada ya mavuno

### Chokaa

Weka chokaa kabla ya mvua nyingi; usichanganye na DAP/CAN siku ya kupandikiza.
